svg.text: Describe every fracture film in the same order
Detect it first: trace the cortex, look for secondary signs
1 · Views · 2 · Location · 3 · Type · 4 · Descriptors · 5 · Joint surface · 6 · Other findings · 7 · Bone quality · 8 · Healing
• More than one descriptor for each fracture
• OLD ACIDS: Open or closed · Location · Degree (complete or incomplete) · Articular surface · Comminution and type · Intrinsic bone quality · Displacement · Soft tissue
STANDARD VIEWS: AP · lateral · oblique, the body described in anatomic position
• An oblique fracture shows on one view
• A spiral fracture needs multiple views
RIGHT OR LEFT · WHICH BONE · WHICH PART
• Epiphysis (end) · physis (growth plate, immature skeleton only)
• Non-articular bump where muscles or tendons attach, under traction
COMPLETE (all the way through), by the fracture line
• Straight across, perpendicular to the shaft
• Check a second view to tell from spiral
• Winds around the shaft: twisting injury
• Needs multiple views · can resemble oblique, with a butterfly fragment
THE DISTAL FRAGMENT RELATIVE TO THE PROXIMAL
Except the clavicle: there the proximal fragment is described relative to the distal (neck muscles pull it up).
• Ends move away from each other, in shaft widths
• Translation more than a full shaft width
• Named by the direction of the apex
• Varus = apex lateral · valgus = apex medial
LENGTH (and rotation: turned internally or externally, so look at the joints above and below)
Intra-articular: risk of secondary osteoarthritis, the reduction must be anatomic, longer to heal.
• Abrupt break in the joint's cortical line: trace the
• = an intra-articular fracture even when no line is
• Through the skin: the lecture's case,
upper and mid third of the tibia and fibula
• Fracture around an implant · note any foreign body or hardware
• A tendon or ligament pulls off a fragment
triangle at the extensor tendon's base of
• Widened or incongruent joint, with or without fracture
• Its own finding, named in the description
HEALING IS A CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS: no tenderness, no motion at the fracture site, weight-bearing possible
• Complete secondary healing years after the fracture
• Line widens at 10-14 days (resorption, not displacement)
• Callus at 2 weeks · union = mature bridging callus, medullary
• Upper limb 3-10 weeks (distal humerus longest) · lower limb
• Delayed union = twice as long as expected · non-union = no
healing in 6-9 months · malunion = non-anatomic healing
